question: Why did completion candidates disappear in the B4-A and B5-A harder cohorts?

representation.completion: any state attaining the deterministic landscape global optimum
representation.ceiling: a target landscape has no completion state inside the frozen representation

operator.grammar: one-field adjacent numeric move or categorical destination from legal_adjacent_moves
operator.operator_distance: shortest grammar path to a completion state, allowing neutral/downhill states
operator.strict_admissible_distance: shortest grammar path whose every edge strictly increases frozen score
operator.ceiling: a target initial state lacks either a grammar path or a strict-admissible path
operator.historical_dead_end_rule: loss of strict reachability after an initially supported path is reported as generation path loss, not retroactively called initial operator non-support

generation.coverage_ceiling: all target landscapes have initial strict-admissible completion paths, but zero target trajectories generate any completion candidate
generation.completion_directed: generated candidate has smaller strict-admissible distance than its current parent and is strictly retainable
generation.exact_oracle_edge: generated candidate is a legal strict neighbor with distance exactly parent_distance-1
generation.claim_boundary: coverage ceiling of the frozen historical generation setup, not intrinsic model incapacity

claim_ceiling: deterministic finite-space and consumed-trajectory routing evidence only; no new mechanism effectiveness, causal model limitation, generalization, safety, device, or admission claim
